description:
FILED s540 (the reviewing session, 2026-11-13) on the USER's word (paraphrased): run the CPAN modules in use to compare speed, then find out where PCL is slower, and make a list of things that should be faster.  This is the first concrete piece of #4621 (the benchmarking of real programs the USER announced in s536); #4788 is its sibling (the review of everything the CPAN runs do not reach).

WHAT TO MEASURE
1. POPULATION: the CPAN board, 30 distributions / 896 test files (baselines/cpan-board-dists.tsv), each file run from its distribution's directory as the board runs it (tools/run-dist-t.pl); only files that run to their plan under PCL count for the comparison (641 at the s539 round) -- a file that stops early does less work and would read as fast.
2. PER FILE, perl and PCL: wall time and CPU time, and for PCL the three phases SEPARATELY -- transpile (pl2cl, incl. the modules it loads), load / compile of the emitted Lisp, and the RUN.  Warm module cache and cold, stated which.  The comparison is in ABSOLUTE seconds (Target A, feedback_speed_absolute_not_ratio): a 40x ratio on a 5 ms file matters less than 2x on a 20 s one.  Report both the sum and the per-file table.
3. A QUIET BOX: timing legs are exclusive (heavy.sh KIND bench); a run taken while other legs run is void.  Repeat each timing at least twice and report the spread; the s539 round showed load alone turns 30 s files into 120 s timeouts.
4. WHERE: for the files that hold the most absolute excess time (the top ~20 by PCL seconds minus perl seconds, and separately the top by run-phase excess), profile the RUN with the SBCL statistical profiler (sb-sprof, :cpu and :alloc) and name the functions and the Perl constructs behind them; profile the compile phase of the slowest-compiling modules separately (docs/parser-review-s525.md measured 46 % of compile time in PPI::Node::find, docs/codegen-review-s526.md 60.5 % in PPI).
5. THE LIST (the deliverable): docs/cpan-speed-comparison-sNNN.md -- the per-distribution table, then one row per THING THAT SHOULD BE FASTER: what it is (construct / runtime function / compile pass), how many seconds over how many files it holds, the suspected lever, a cheap discriminating measurement that would confirm it, and a size guess.  Ranked by measured seconds.  Each row that is a real lever is FILED as its own task with the measurement; nothing is fixed in this task.

KNOWN INPUTS (do not re-derive; confirm or refute with the new numbers): #4621's list (#4061 the weak-table write per bless; #4305 deref overloads +93 % once any class registers one); docs/method-lookup-eval-s534.md (inherited method calls 3.9-7.4x perl, #4523-#4525 awaiting the USER); docs/speed-review-s509.md (start-up 53 ms warm; #2770-#2773); #477 (pos loop quadratic); #4643 (heap exhaustion compiling a huge sub); docs/where-the-time-goes.md, docs/faster-codegen-suggestions.md.

BAR: no code change, so no gate / sweep; the doc, the raw tables under baselines/ or the scratch directory named in the doc, and the filed tasks.  Flag any file where PCL is FASTER than perl by more than 2x: that is usually a file doing less work (a silent skip), i.e. a correctness finding.
subject: SPEED (USER s540): run the CPAN distributions PCL uses (the board) under perl and under PCL, compare the time file by file, find out WHERE PCL is slower, and make the list of things that should be faster
